missions.title: Retire slashing: SlashJudge, SlashAppeal, slash escrow and the unbonding window
missions.description:
## Summary

The protocol has no slashable offense left once rate-manipulation slashing and blacklist slashing go. Remove the slashing machinery and everything that exists only to support it.

## Why

- `CapacityBond.slash` is gated by `SLASH_ROLE`, and only `SlashJudge` holds that role.
- `SlashJudge` has two offenses. `RateManipulation` goes with the voucher-less stream open that replaces `cdn/probe/v1`. `Blacklist` goes with the reduction of `ContentBlacklist` to regional tag lists. After both, `SlashJudge` adjudicates nothing.
- The 14-day unbonding window exists only to outlast the slash evidence window (ADR 026 § Capacity-bond curve, ADR 014 § Interaction with unbonding period). With no slash, it protects nothing.

## Scope

- **Contracts.** Delete `SlashJudge`, `ISlashJudge`, `SlashAppeal`, `SlashEscrowLib`. In `CapacityBond`: delete `slash`, the tier ladder (`SLASH_BPS_TIER_*`), `lifetimeOffenseCount`, escrow-on-slash and `finalizeUnappealedSlash`, `SLASH_ROLE`, `SLASH_APPEAL_ROLE` and the settle hooks, the `slashJudge` evidence-age pointer, and the `MAX_EVIDENCE_AGE_US < unbondingPeriod` cross-check. Delete the unbonding window: an exit is immediate. In `DecdnGovernor`: delete `_slashedInWindow` and the slash zero-out of vote weight.
- **Rust.** Delete the node `slash_watcher` and the `incentive` bindings for `SlashJudge` and `SlashAppeal`. Remove slash metrics.
- **CLI.** Delete `decdn appeal slash`. Simplify `unbond` to an immediate exit.
- **Docs.** Move ADR 028 to `adr/_history/`. ADR 014: move the secp256k1 EIP-712 `StreamResponse` signature scheme to ADR 005 (clients and origin attestations still use it) and retire the slashing-evidence part. ADR 026: remove § Slashing and burn and the unbonding rules. ADR 036: remove § Slashing zero-out and § Slashed-but-still-voting. ADR 009: remove slash-appeal authorization. Update `adr/architecture.md`, the glossary, CLAUDE.md (the "bounty-slash" key design decision) and the observability appendix.

## Ordering

This lands after the stream-open change that retires rate-manipulation slashing and after the `ContentBlacklist` reduction that retires blacklist slashing.

Pre-mainnet, so the change is ABI-breaking with no compatibility path.

missions.title: Run a structured attack pass on the Codex reader and file what it finds
missions.description:
## Now

The reader’s suite passes. Outside challengers found wrong reports, and two same-owner dry runs found cases the tests missed. In both dry runs the reader gave the correct answer at `27b77dd`. Earlier internal reviews had no list of classes to try or rule for what counts as a break. We cannot tell which classes have been tried. [Saved-approval test gap](https://github.com/chalkbadger/stay-safe/issues/107) · [System-rules test gap](https://github.com/chalkbadger/stay-safe/issues/108)

## Change

Add a skill to stay-safe that lists four classes of cases for the Codex reader. Run it once. For each attempt, write a synthetic config, establish what the pinned Codex version does from its source or an existing recorded run, and compare that with the reader’s report.

| Class | Starting point |
| --- | --- |
| One setting cancels another in the same file | `features.apps = false` beside an `[apps.*]` table. [Accepted challenge](https://github.com/chalkbadger/stay-safe/issues/109#issuecomment-6999572959) |
| Saved approvals | Incident I26 and [#107](https://github.com/chalkbadger/stay-safe/issues/107). |
| Configured programs | Hooks, MCP servers and `notify`. Use the public behavior reported in [openai/codex#62485](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/62485) as a starting point and check what the pinned source establishes. |
| Values Codex reads differently from the reader | Wrong types and legacy aliases, starting with `features.connectors`. |

## After

I open the checkout with a coding agent and ask for the pass. It works through the four classes using synthetic files. It runs `python3 -m stay_safe --config FILE` and leaves configured programs untouched. I get a table showing each input, the expected behavior and its source, what stay-safe reported, and one of three verdicts:

- **Break.** The reader gives a wrong answer about behavior it claims to cover.
- **Declared gap.** The report tells the user which behavior it did not check.
- **Correct.** The report agrees with the pinned behavior on the point being checked.

For each reader mismatch, I get a filled challenge form to review and file. Suspected vulnerabilities go through the [private reporting channel](https://github.com/chalkbadger/stay-safe/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

## Success

The PR publishes these observations for the reader pass:

- Every class has at least one attempt. The run record gives its synthetic config, Codex citation or existing recorded run, stay-safe output and verdict. Details of suspected vulnerabilities stay in the private report.
- At `27b77dd`, the pass re-finds the accepted `features.apps = false` case. That gives reviewers a known wrong answer against which to check the method.
- Each new reader mismatch is filed through the challenge form and labelled `same-owner`. The run record links the filing, or the existing challenge for a known case.

## Not included

- Fixes to the reader. Each fix gets its own issue. This pass changes nothing under `stay_safe/` and changes no contract claim.
- Permission profiles and the network proxy, which need reader support first.
- Settings spread across multiple config files.
- Work under pending disclosure.
- Instruction files such as `AGENTS.md`.
- Other agents.
- Bounty terms and reopening.

missions.title: F-10 — Money-path ledger integrity: refunds never claw back, quest payouts re-arm (High)
missions.description:
# F-10 — Money-path ledger integrity: refunds never claw back, quest payouts re-arm (High)

**Consolidates:** issues [#23](../issues/issue23-stripe-refunds-never-reverse-pollen.md) (Stripe refunds/lost chargebacks never reverse credited Pollen) and [#116](../issues/issue116-quest-pr-payout-rearm.md) (quest-bounty PR payouts re-arm on body edit) — 2 issues, one surface: **the USD↔Pollen ledger has no negative feedback — money can enter twice or leave zero times.**

**Status on upstream `main` @ `4e662050` — re-verified by code inspection 2026-11-19:** `stripe-webhooks.ts:841-865` still handles `refund.created/updated/failed` as log + Tinybird analytics only (no `pack_balance` write anywhere in the refund path); the quest payout path still records quest payments only under `github:issue:N` (the `github:merged_pr:N` id appears in the *check* list but is never added to the *earned* set when a quest pays — the re-arm window stays open).

**Fix PRs:** [#27](https://github.com/NamanSoni78/pollinationsai/pull/27), [#131](https://github.com/NamanSoni78/pollinationsai/pull/131).

---

## What this chain can do, end to end

**Refund fraud (issue 23) — repeatable per purchase, no maintainer involvement:**
```
buy $100 pack  ->  100 Pollen credited (checkout.session.completed)
spend the Pollen (generations, keys, transfers)
request a Stripe refund / force a lost chargeback
  -> USD returns to the attacker
  -> Pollen stays; spent Pollen stays; credited Pollen silently diverges from collected USD
```
Every `pack_balance` write in the repo is a *credit* — repo-wide there is no reversal path. `charge.dispute.*` falls to the unhandled `default`. The fraud-ban tooling only bans access; it never claws back. Partially mitigated by the hourly fraud score (one "fraudulent" dispute scores 0.39 < the 0.75 ban threshold; non-fraudulent reasons score 0 forever) and 3DS only for first purchases / packs < $10.

**Quest payout re-arm (issue 116) — one merged PR pays K+1 times:**
```
open quests 9600@$10, 9601@$25, 9602@$10 (descending rewards)
merge PR 9951 closing 9601  ->  pays $25 (recorded ONLY under github:issue:9601)
edit the PR body (post-payout, post-merge) to close 9602 instead
  -> ids checked = [github:merged_pr:9951, github:issue:9602]
  -> earned has github:issue:9601 only  ->  PAYS AGAIN
strip the reference entirely  ->  the default merged-PR card pays $5 more
```
Payment multiplicity is fully attacker-controlled (GitHub derives closing references from the PR body, which the author can always edit); amounts are maintainer-bounded. **2026-11-19 code check:** upstream's `ids` list includes `github:merged_pr:N` (from #19983, 2026-11-17) but the quest-payment branch still records only the quest's id — the marker never enters the earned set, so the re-arm window is open exactly as reported.

## Proof

**issue 23 — integration suite over the signed webhook route (real D1/migrations, mocked Stripe API), contract pinned on the fix branch:**
- full refund debits exactly once; duplicate webhook replay idempotent by refund id
- partials scale + cumulative clamp; pending refund reverses nothing
- lost dispute reverses; won dispute keeps the credit
- and the gap established on unpatched HEAD: **none of these events touch `pack_balance` at all**
- 105/105 + 58/58 suites green; migration `0083`
- The policy decision the original design-gap note (R3-D1) requested is implemented in the PR: debit into negative balance (the platform's documented overdraft semantics), quest rewards deliberately untouched, ops-initiated reversals unaffected.

**issue 116 — unit red/green on the existing Miniflare + GitHub-mock harness (PR state mutated the way a body edit would):**
```
seed quests 9600@10 / 9601@25 / 9602@10; PR 9951 pays 25
mock body-edit (closingIssues [] -> [9602])
  unpatched main: re-pays at each step           (RED)
  with fix: pre-claimed github:merged_pr:9951 marker -> no new row, ever
```

## Members & fixes

| Issue | One-line | Verification | Fork PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 23 | Stripe refunds and lost chargebacks never reverse credited Pollen | Integration (4 tests; unpatched gap established) | [#27](https://github.com/NamanSoni78/pollinationsai/pull/27) |
| 116 | Quest PR payouts re-arm by editing the merged PR's closing references | Unit red/green (body-edit simulated) | [#131](https://github.com/NamanSoni78/pollinationsai/pull/131) |

## Merge guidance

1. **#27** implements a policy (debit-into-negative on refund/dispute) that was explicitly deferred to maintainers — the PR is the decision; review the semantics, not just the code.
2. **#131** ships a one-row pre-claim marker plus a documented residual (PRs merged *before* deploy can re-arm once more without a D1 backfill — the PR names it).
3. Related but separate: the overdraft/settle-floor questions live in **F-05**; the sandbox/x402 credential axes in **F-09**.

missions.title: [Bug Bounty] The concentration panel prints eight 0.12² terms as equal to 0.1250
missions.description:
The Concentration tab prints an equation that a reader cannot reproduce from its displayed operands. For eight equally weighted holdings, the app prints eight terms of 0.12² and gives their sum as 0.1250. Their sum is 0.1152. The engine correctly uses eight weights of 0.125 internally and calculates an HHI of 0.125 and eight effective assets. The discrepancy is in the displayed derivation.

## Inputs

In the custom portfolio, use MSFT, AAPL, JPM, COST, GLD, XOM, TSLA and AMD. Give each holding a weight of 12.5%. An equivalent way to obtain the weights is to enter 1 for each of the eight rows and click “Normalize to 100%”. Open Concentration and expand “Mathematical derivation (HHI & Effective Assets)”.

| Holdings | Terms shown | Sum from those terms | Result shown |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Eight at 12.5% each | Eight × 0.12² | 0.1152 | 0.1250 |
| Four at 25% each | Four × 0.25² | 0.2500 | 0.2500 |

## Why it happens

The panel formats each fractional weight to two decimal places before printing it. The exact binary fraction 0.125 formats as 0.12 in Python. By contrast, the right-hand side comes from the engine using the original weights. In the eight-holding case, even the displayed operands add up to only 0.96.

```python
from decimal import Decimal

weight = Decimal("0.125")
printed_weight = Decimal(f"{float(weight):.2f}")
assert 8 * printed_weight**2 == Decimal("0.1152")
assert 8 * weight**2 == Decimal("0.125")
```

I ran the published concentration function and its original Markdown-rendering block in browser-hosted Python with pandas. I captured the exact equation passed to Streamlit for both rows above. This check covers the calculation and the displayed equation text. It did not exercise the live site's form controls.

Printing 0.125 for these holdings makes the illustrated derivation agree with its result. For weights with more digits than the UI displays, an approximation sign or a rounding note can keep the equation accurate. This report concerns a display logic error.

This AI-assisted report is submitted for consideration under the project's logic-error bounty. Please confirm eligibility if accepted.

[Concentration panel](https://github.com/Ayush441-python/AUREN/blob/eef89475dece13ad243c6fc83d06f0ae1d1b0882/app.py#L492-L499) · [Concentration calculation](https://github.com/Ayush441-python/AUREN/blob/eef89475dece13ad243c6fc83d06f0ae1d1b0882/engine/metrics.py#L11-L19)

missions.title: Embedded images: local URLs with a query string or percent-encoding are not embedded
missions.description:
### Mautic Series 7.2.x series ### Mautic installed version 7.2.2 (also 7.x HEAD `e323d688a2`) ### Way of installing I cloned the Mautic repo ### PHP version 8.5 ### What browsers are you seeing the problem on? Not relevant (server-side) ### What happened? With `mailer_convert_embed_images` enabled, `convertEmbedImages()` maps a URL starting with `site_url` to a local path by plain string replace (`MailHelper.php:855-857`). The query string and percent-encoding are kept, so the file is not found and the image is silently left as a remote URL: - Theme assets from `getAssetUrl()` have a cache buster: `/themes//assets/logo.png?v1a2b3c4d` -> looks for a file named `logo.png?v1a2b3c4d`. - Media files with spaces: `/media/images/My%20File.png` -> looks for `My%20File.png` instead of `My File.png`. Since 7.2.0 the read error is suppressed (`@file_get_contents`), so the send continues but the image is not embedded. Before 7.2.0 the warning aborted the whole send. ### How can we reproduce this issue? 1. Enable "Convert embed images to Base64". 2. Put `media/images/My File.png` on the server. 3. Create an email with: `` `` 4. Send it and check the raw message: both src values are still remote URLs, no image parts. Expected: query string and fragment are stripped and the path is URL-decoded before the file lookup, and both images are embedded.

missions.title: Embedded images missing for every batch after the first when "Convert embed images to Base64" is on
missions.description:
### Mautic Series 7.2.x series ### Mautic installed version 7.2.2 (also 7.x HEAD `e323d688a2`) ### Way of installing I cloned the Mautic repo ### PHP version 8.5 ### What browsers are you seeing the problem on? Not relevant (server-side) ### What happened? With `mailer_convert_embed_images` enabled, only the first `sendEmail()` call in a process gets the image parts. Contacts in later batches receive HTML with `src="cid:"` but no matching MIME part, so the images are broken. Cause: `MailHelper::$embedImagesReplaces` (URL -> `cid:` map) is never cleared. `reset(true)` creates a new message (`MailHelper.php:641`), and `SendEmailToContact::setEmail()` calls it via `flush()` for each batch. On the next batch, `convertEmbedImages()` applies the old map first (`:839`), then skips every `cid:` src (`:844`), so `embed()` is never called on the new message. This affects any long-running process that reuses MailHelper: broadcast batches, several broadcasts in one cron run, `mautic:campaigns:trigger`. Same symptom as the old #9003 and #9819. ### How can we reproduce this issue? 1. Enable Configuration > Email Settings > "Convert embed images to Base64". 2. Create a segment email with ``, segment with 4 contacts. 3. Run `bin/console mautic:broadcasts:send -i --batch=2`. 4. Check the raw messages (e.g. in Mailpit): - Contacts 1-2: `multipart/related`, image part attached, `src="cid:@symfony"`. - Contacts 3-4: only `multipart/alternative`, no image part, `src="cid:"` - broken image. missions.title: [Bug Bounty] ai_report() sends Groq/reasoning-only parameters (include_reasoning, reasoning_effort) to non-reasoning models and non-Groq providers
missions.description:
## Summary

`engine/report.py::ai_report()` documents support for any OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint (Groq, OpenAI, Ollama, OpenRouter), but its request payload builder misclassifies models and sends unsupported reasoning parameters in three cases:

1. **Non-reasoning models on Groq** (e.g., `llama-3.3-70b-versatile`, `llama-3.1-8b-instant`): `"groq.com" in base_url` forces `reasoning = True`, unconditionally sending Groq's reasoning-only `include_reasoning: false` and `reasoning_effort: "low"` (which Groq's `/openai/v1/chat/completions` endpoint rejects with HTTP 400 `invalid_request_error` on standard Llama models) and dropping the `system` message role.
2. **Non-reasoning models on OpenAI / Ollama / OpenRouter** (e.g., `gpt-4o-mini`, `llama3.2`): even when `reasoning` evaluates to `False`, `payload["reasoning_effort"] = effort` runs outside `if reasoning:`, sending `reasoning_effort` to models that reject it.
3. **`gpt-oss` on non-Groq providers** (e.g., OpenRouter / OpenAI-compatible endpoints): `"gpt-oss" in model` sends Groq-specific `include_reasoning: false` to endpoints outside `groq.com`.

## Affected Upstream Commit
`eef89475dece13ad243c6fc83d06f0ae1d1b0882`

## Supported Input / Workflow
- Streamlit dashboard **AI Report** tab (`app.py:856-875`) calling `ai_report(metrics, base_url, api_key, model)` with any non-`gpt-oss` Groq model (e.g., `LLM_MODEL=llama-3.3-70b-versatile`), OpenAI (`gpt-4o-mini`), or Ollama (`llama3.2` from `.env.example`).
- Direct calls to `engine.report.ai_report()`.

## Minimal Reproduction (Offline, No API Key)

Run from the repository root:

```python
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch
from engine.report import ai_report

metrics = {"risk_score": 70, "risk_level": "High"}
cases = [
    ("Groq Llama", "https://api.groq.com/openai/v1", "gsk-test", "llama-3.3-70b-versatile"),
    ("OpenAI gpt-4o-mini", "https://api.openai.com/v1", "sk-test", "gpt-4o-mini"),
    ("Ollama llama3.2", "http://localhost:11434/v1", "", "llama3.2"),
    ("OpenRouter gpt-oss", "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1", "or-test", "openai/gpt-oss-120b"),
]

for label, url, key, model in cases:
    resp = MagicMock(ok=True)
    resp.json.return_value = {"choices": [{"message": {"content": "Score is 70."}}]}
    with patch("engine.report.requests.post", return_value=resp) as mock_post:
        ai_report(metrics, url, key, model)
        p = mock_post.call_args.kwargs["json"]
    print(
        label,
        "-> include_reasoning:", p.get("include_reasoning"),
        "reasoning_effort:", p.get("reasoning_effort"),
        "roles:", [m["role"] for m in p["messages"]],
    )
```

## Expected Result
- Non-reasoning models (`llama-3.3-70b-versatile`, `gpt-4o-mini`, `llama3.2`): neither `include_reasoning` nor `reasoning_effort` is sent; `messages` uses `["system", "user"]` with `max_tokens: 1500`.
- `openai/gpt-oss-120b` on non-Groq endpoints: `include_reasoning` is omitted.
- Default Groq + `openai/gpt-oss-120b`: unchanged (`include_reasoning: false`, `reasoning_effort: "low"`, `max_completion_tokens: 4096`).

## Actual Result
```text
Groq Llama -> include_reasoning: False reasoning_effort: low roles: ['user']
OpenAI gpt-4o-mini -> include_reasoning: None reasoning_effort: low roles: ['system', 'user']
Ollama llama3.2 -> include_reasoning: None reasoning_effort: low roles: ['system', 'user']
OpenRouter gpt-oss -> include_reasoning: False reasoning_effort: low roles: ['user']
```

## Root Cause
In [`engine/report.py` (lines 34–53)](https://github.com/Ayush441-python/AUREN/blob/eef89475dece13ad243c6fc83d06f0ae1d1b0882/engine/report.py#L34-L53):
- Line 34 sets `reasoning = "gpt-oss" in (model or "") or "groq.com" in (base_url or "")`, conflating the Groq host with reasoning models.
- Line 42 sets `payload["include_reasoning"] = False` unconditionally inside `if reasoning:`, even for non-Groq endpoints.
- Lines 51–53 attach `payload["reasoning_effort"] = effort` unconditionally outside `if reasoning:`.

## User Impact
Users configuring AUREN's AI Report tab with standard Groq models (`llama-3.3-70b-versatile`, `llama-3.1-8b-instant`) or non-reasoning OpenAI models (`gpt-4o`, `gpt-4o-mini`) receive HTTP 400 errors from the provider API instead of a generated risk report, even when `LLM_REASONING_EFFORT` is unset on Groq (because `include_reasoning` is hardcoded).

## Duplicate Check
- #113 (and PRs #115, #123) covers `engine/env.py::load_env()` shadowing Streamlit secrets with `os.environ.setdefault(...)`. Neither PR modifies `engine/report.py`; even with #113 fixed, `ai_report()` still unconditionally sends `include_reasoning: false` for all `groq.com` models and `reasoning_effort` for non-reasoning models whenever `LLM_REASONING_EFFORT` is configured.
- #112 (and PRs #116, #122) covers `clean_output()` unclosed `<think>` tags and `finish_reason == "length"`.
- #64, #65, #93, #110 cover stale snapshots and `unverified_numbers()`.

## Suggested Fix
Gate `reasoning` on the model (`"gpt-oss" in (model or "").lo

missions.title: Womier M87 Pro: hardware details, bootloader access, and looking for a stock firmware dump
missions.description:
Hi! Thanks for building M87 Control. It's great to see someone else digging into this keyboard. I've been researching my own M87 Pro and wanted to share what I found in case it helps, and to ask if you've come across anything similar. My unit PCB: DYH830-RGB-HFD BT/2.4G V4.0, dated 2024/08/12 USB: 05AC:024F, REV_0138 (firmware V1.38) MCU: HFD80CP100 (U5, SONiX SN32F299 clone), 256 KB flash Wireless: WCH CH582F + 32 MHz crystal SPI flash: PUYA PY25Q128HA (U7, 16 MB, holds the screen art) RTC: U11 + 32.768 kHz crystal Display: 240×135, ST7789 (per the driver config) Bootloader access works There are two unlabelled round through‑hole pads just right of the MCU. With the battery unplugged, shorting them while plugging in USB enters the SONiX ROM bootloader (0C45:7140). sonixflasher -v 0c45/7140 -i reports: Device: SN32F29X, ROM 256 KB, Security level: CS1, Code option: 0x0000 Flash checksum: 0x7b49 So there's always a hardware recovery path, but code security is on, so the firmware can't be read back through the bootloader. Things to avoid The updater bundled with the Womier M87 Pro driver (SI-2195 ... F98 Pro ... HFD80CP100_V1.20 ... 0x4ACA.exe) actually contains AULA F98 Pro firmware (0C45:800A, 95 keys). It isn't for the M87 Pro. The DP25125_X147C ... HFD80CP100_V1.13 ... 0xA192.exe on Womier's site is Womier WK98 firmware, but it targets the same 05AC:024F ID. Please don't run either of these on an M87 Pro. What I'm after I'd like to change the display behaviour: make volume the default page and blank the screen after ~5 s idle. As far as I can tell, the vendor protocol has no commands for this, which matches your findings. That means firmware work, and I don't want to do that without a backup. Have you, or anyone following this repo, come across: an official M87 Pro / DYH830 firmware updater? The XVX driver references 德亿宏DYH830_87键_三模_RGB_彩屏_HFD80CP100_V1.13_20230424.exe, but it isn't published anywhere I can find, and Womier and XVX support haven't replied. any SWD dump of an M87 Pro? A good dump should have a 16‑bit little‑endian word sum matching what the bootloader reports, so it would be easy to verify. Happy to share photos, the extracted vendor images, or anything else useful. Thanks!

missions.title: Recover from revoked or missing eventsubs instead of silently dropping firsts
missions.description:
## Problem

If Twitch revokes or drops a broadcaster's channel points eventsub, the EBS stops recording firsts for that channel silently and permanently, until the broadcaster happens to re-save the extension config.

- The eventsub is only created in `/eventsub/create` (`update_eventsub` in `ebs/verifiedfirst/twitch.py`), which the config page calls when the broadcaster saves.
- The `revocation` branch of `/eventsub` in `ebs/verifiedfirst/main/routes.py` only calls `twitch.delete_eventsub` and logs the subscription id. It doesn't log *why* the subscription was revoked, doesn't recreate it, and leaves `broadcaster.eventsub_id` pointing at a dead subscription.
- If the callback was unreachable when Twitch revoked the subscription (e.g. `notification_failures_exceeded` during an EBS outage), the revocation message may never arrive at all. Nothing ever notices that the subscription is gone.

This is the most likely cause of #317: the broadcaster's firsts stopped for ~7 weeks and resumed only after they re-saved the config, which created a new eventsub.

## Proposed change

### 1. Log the revocation reason

In the `revocation` branch, log `subscription.status` (the revocation reason: `user_removed`, `authorization_revoked`, `notification_failures_exceeded`, `version_removed`) along with `broadcaster_id`, `eventsub_id` and `reward_id` at WARNING level.

### 2. Recreate the eventsub on revocation where it makes sense

After handling the revocation, if all of the following hold:
- the broadcaster exists in the database,
- the revoked subscription is the broadcaster's current one (`subscription.id == broadcaster.eventsub_id`) and its `condition.reward_id` matches `broadcaster.reward_id`, so stale or test-instance subscriptions are ignored,
- the reason is recoverable (`notification_failures_exceeded`, `version_removed`),

then call `twitch.update_eventsub(broadcaster, broadcaster.reward_id)`. That function already deletes non-matching subscriptions and creates a new one with this instance's callback, and it stores the new id.

For `authorization_revoked` and `user_removed`, don't recreate, because it would fail and is not wanted. Clear `broadcaster.eventsub_id` so the database reflects reality.

Recreation failures (`RequestException`) must be caught and logged. The handler still has to return 2xx to Twitch for the revocation message. Creating a subscription is async on Twitch's side (it returns `webhook_callback_verification_pending` and verifies the callback afterwards), so calling it from inside the webhook handler won't deadlock.

### 3. Reconcile subscriptions periodically

The revocation handler alone doesn't cover the case where the revocation message is never delivered. Add a script, e.g. `ebs/scripts/reconcile_eventsubs.py` and runnable as `python -m scripts.reconcile_eventsubs` like the existing scripts, that:

- lists all of the app's eventsubs with `GET /eventsub/subscriptions`, following the `pagination.cursor`. There are several hundred broadcasters, so it must not be one request per broadcaster.
- for every broadcaster with a non-empty `reward_id`, checks for an `enabled` subscription for that reward whose `transport.callback` equals `EVENTSUB_CALLBACK_URL`.
- if there isn't one, calls `update_eventsub` for that broadcaster and logs what it did. If it fails (e.g. the broadcaster revoked access), logs and continues with the next broadcaster.
- supports `--dry-run`, which reports what it would change without creating or deleting anything.
- prints a summary (checked / ok / recreated / failed).
- only touches subscriptions whose callback matches this instance's `EVENTSUB_CALLBACK_URL`. The client id is shared with the test deployment (see 183d832c), so the script must not delete the test instance's subscriptions and vice versa.

Scheduling it (e.g. a systemd timer in jaedolph-infra-deploy) is out of scope for this issue. Mention in the PR how it's meant to be run.

## Tests

Add tests in `ebs/tests/test_main.py` and `ebs/tests/test_twitch.py` (or a new test module for the script) following the existing mocker-based style (see `test_eventsub_revocation`):

- a revocation logs the reason
- a `notification_failures_exceeded` revocation for the current subscription recreates it
- an `authorization_revoked` revocation does not recreate and clears `eventsub_id`
- a revocation for a subscription that isn't the broadcaster's current one doesn't recreate
- a recreation failure still returns 2xx
- reconciliation: missing/disabled subscription → recreated; subscription at another callback is left alone; dry run changes nothing; pagination is followed

Run `tox` in `ebs/` before opening the PR.

missions.title: bug(crud): curated-template not-found guard raises TypeError instead of 404
missions.description:
**Found while auditing duplicated not-found guards (Phase 1 of the line-reduction programme).**

`backend/app/crud/dweller.py:745` raises the not-found exception with the identifier only:

```python
template = game_data_store.get_dweller(template_id)
if template is None:
    raise ResourceNotFoundException(template_id)
```

`ResourceNotFoundException.__init__` is `(self, model: type[SQLModel], identifier: str | UUID, identifier_type: str = "id", headers=None)` — it requires a model class as the first positional argument. So this raise executes as `model=template_id` with no `identifier`, which raises `TypeError` inside the constructor rather than the intended 404.

**Effect:** a curated dweller template that exists in a caller's reference but not in `game_data_store` produces a 500 from the reward path instead of a 404 with a useful detail. The call is inside `build_curated_template`, which locks the vault row first, so the failure also happens after a lock is taken.

**Fix:**

```python
raise ResourceNotFoundException(DwellerTemplate, identifier=template_id)
```

(or whichever model type `game_data_store.get_dweller` returns), plus a regression test that asserts 404 rather than 500 when the template id is unknown.

Not fixed in the refactor PR because it is a behaviour change (500 → 404) and that PR is scoped to construction-only edits.

Two ₱5 coins dropped back to back arrive as one 10-pulse train and earn the ₱10 tier; dropped with a pause they earn the ₱5 tier twice (ADR-0070). If the ₱10 bonus is more than twice the ₱5 bonus, the defaults reward fast insertion. Worth keeping in mind when picking the two values.

missions.title: Questions about reproducing
missions.description:
Hi, thank you for releasing IG-Clarifier!

**Summary.** We are reproducing Table 1 (Qwen3-1.7B clarifier, τ-bench retail + airline). With the released code, the clarifier learns to ask at nearly every turn. After changing three settings in the reward pipeline, we reproduce the drop in clarifications (−50 to −60% vs. Baseline), but not the SR gain. We found a few places where the released code and the paper seem to differ. We would like to know which version Table 1 used. Details are below the questions.

## Questions
**Main**
1. **User simulator.** Was Table 1 trained with the released simulator generation: the prompt fed as raw text without a chat template, and 128 new tokens? If not, what prompt format and generation settings did you use?
2. **Reward history window.** The scorer sees only the first 1,600 characters of the history (`IG_MAX_HISTORY_LENGTH`), while the policy sees the last 1,400 tokens. Was the scorer limited this way for the paper? Also, did the training prompts use `Context: … Your task:` (what the regex expects) or `History:` (the paper's prompt)?
3. **Abstentions.** The released code uses 6 of 8 rollouts, picks question rollouts first, and masks abstentions out of the loss. For Table 1, were abstentions masked this way, or kept with reward 0 (our reading of §3 and §5)?
4. **Evaluation loop** (not in the repo).
   - How are the clarifier's question and the user's answer inserted into the agent's context?
   - Is the clarifier called after every tool call?
   - Which thinking mode did the agent and user use, and what was the max step count?
   - Could you share the evaluation script?

**Minor**

5. Is the mean reward in Fig. 3(b) (≈0.15 at step 200) computed over question rollouts only, or does it include abstentions?
6. Which verl version did you use?

## Details
### Setup
- This repo @ `4071af1`, verl `v0.5.0`, τ-bench @ `59a200c`. Same models as the paper.
- Differences from the paper in all runs:
  - 300 training steps (not 670)
  - max response 2048 (not 1760)
  - 1 evaluation trial (not 3)
- Our own evaluation loop: the clarifier runs after every tool call. Its question goes into the agent's context as an assistant message and the user's answer as a user message.
- Two fixes were needed to train at all:
  - The history regex expects `Context: … Your task:`, but the paper's prompt uses `History:`.
  - Rollouts shared one `extra_info` dict, so every rollout in a group got the same reward and the advantage was 0.

### Results
SR (%) is the mean of retail and airline. Clarify is the number of questions per task. Ours uses the step-300 checkpoint.

| Run | Abstentions | User simulator | Scorer history | Prompts/step | Seed | Ours SR / clarify | Baseline SR / clarify | None SR | What happened |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | masked (released) | released | first 1,600 chars (released) | 8 | default | 11.7 / 9.6 | 12.5 / 8.8 | 17.4 | Asks at nearly every turn |
| R2 | in loss, reward 0 | released | first 1,600 chars | 8 | default | 15.0 / 10.0 | 12.1 / 7.4 | 19.7 | Asks at nearly every turn |
| R3 | in loss, reward 0 | modified | first 1,600 chars | 8 | default | 12.7 / **3.2** | 11.1 / 8.0 | 17.6 | Asks less; SR +1.6 (one task) |
| R4 | masked | modified | first 1,600 chars | 16 | default | 10.8 / 12.4 | 11.8 / 8.2 | 19.2 | Asks at every turn; outputs collapse to ~30 tokens |
| R5 | in loss, reward 0 | modified | first 1,600 chars | 16 | default | **18.8** / 10.2 | 11.0 / 8.1 | 18.7 | SR up, but asks more than Baseline |
| R6 | in loss, reward 0 | modified | first 1,600 chars | 8 | 43 | 13.4 / 9.8 | 14.0 / 7.0 | 18.9 | Asks at nearly every turn; 95% of questions restate the goal |
| R7 | in loss, reward 0 | modified | full (same as policy) | 8 | 43 | 14.0 / **4.2** | 14.0 / 8.0 | 19.3 | Asks less; SR = Baseline |
| Paper | | | | 16 | | 17.8 / 1.3 | 14.9 / 4.2 | 15.4 | |

What we take from this:
1. **With the released code, the clarifier learns to always ask** (R1, R2, R4).
2. **With the modified simulator and the full scorer history, the drop in clarifications is reproduced:** −50 to −60% vs. Baseline, compared with −69% in the paper. **But SR does not rise above Baseline** (R3, R7).
3. **Runs vary a lot.** R3 and R6 differ only in the seed, yet give 3.2 vs. 9.8 clarifications. None and Baseline move 2–3 points between runs. So single-run SR gaps such as R5's are not conclusive.
4. **In our evaluation, asking hurts.** None is the best or tied-best condition in every run, and it scores higher than in the paper (17.4–19.7 vs. 15.4). Capping the budget at 1–6 questions never beats None. That is the opposite of Fig. 4, which makes us suspect our evaluation loop differs from yours.

### Why we changed these settings
- **Abstentions.** When abstentions are masked out of the loss, nothing rewards *not* asking. "In loss, reward 0" keeps all 8 rollouts.
- **User simulator.** With the released raw-text generation, about 99% of the "answers" are reasoning text that restates the hidde

missions.title: Restaurants without a cuisine tag: let users say which country's food they serve
missions.description:
Mangiamundo only knows a restaurant if OSM gives it a `cuisine` that maps to a country. The Overpass query requires the tag (`[\"cuisine\"]` in `providers/osm.rs`), so a restaurant tagged only `amenity=restaurant` + `name` never shows up, even when it is plainly Ethiopian or Peruvian. Many places are like that, so this hides a lot of food.

## Proposal

- **Fetch them:** the import and the live area queries also fetch restaurant, fast food, café, pub and bar elements with a name but no `cuisine` (`[!\"cuisine\"]`). Store them apart from the playable places (for example a `cuisine IS NULL` row in `osm_places`, never in `place_countries`), so they don't count for discover or the game.
- **Show them:** "Places with unknown food" near the user, nearest first, in a list under the countries (or a section of the add form: "Is it one of these?").
- **Suggest:** "This serves food from…" with the same country picker as the add form, through `POST /api/places/{id}/cuisine` with `{ country }`. Then:
  - post an OSM note at the place: `Cuisine: <name> serves <adjective> food, cuisine=<tag> (via Mangiamundo)`, the way #1 does for missing places;
  - make the place playable **for the suggester** right away (like a pending added place);
  - when **two** users agree on the same country, make it playable for everyone (the same threshold as closed reports);
  - once the import brings the place in with a `cuisine`, OSM wins and the suggestions are dropped.
- **"Nothing specific":** for a snack bar or a Belgian brasserie, the user can say it serves no particular country's food. It is hidden for them, and for everyone after two such answers. No OSM note is posted for this (see below).
- **Limit:** the same daily limit as additions, since each suggestion posts a note.

## Can OSM record that a place has no cuisine?

Not really. The [`cuisine` key](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:cuisine) has no documented value for "none", and OSM generally doesn't map absences. Mappers tag what a place does serve: `regional` or `international`, a local style like `belgian`, or a food type like `burger`, `sandwich` or `friture`. In Mangiamundo those map to no country and are already skipped. So the "nothing specific" answers stay in our own database, and the OSM note for a suggestion is the only thing that reaches OSM.

## Open questions

- Should a confirmed suggestion count for #51-style XP? Probably a small reward, given only once two users agree.
- Hints: rank the list with a guess from the name ("Sushi …" → Japan, "Taj …" → India), shown as a suggestion only and never applied without a user.

missions.title: [trainer, algo] Advantage whitening scope does not match PPO mini-batch update scope
missions.description:
### System Info

- verl: current `main`
- Trainer: V1 `sync` and `colocate_async`
- Advantage estimator: `gae` (also affects `reinforce_plus_plus`, `reinforce_plus_plus_baseline`, and `gdpo`)
- Backend: not specific to FSDP or Megatron
- Hardware: not specific to a particular GPU/NPU model
- Relevant setup: the sampled batch is larger than `ppo_mini_batch_size`; the actor uses token-mean loss and disables auxiliary entropy/KL losses.

### Summary

In the V1 synchronous and colocated trainers, advantages are computed once over the full sampled batch, but the actor update is split into multiple optimizer chunks. For estimators that normalize advantages with `masked_whiten`, this means the whitening scope and the actual optimizer-update scope are different.

The current code path is:

1. `PPOTrainer.step()` sets `sample_batch_size = train_batch_size // parameter_sync_step`. For `trainer_mode=sync`, `parameter_sync_step` defaults to a single local update per step, so the full `train_batch_size` is sampled and used for advantage computation.
2. `_compute_advantage()` computes advantages once over that full sampled batch.
3. For GAE, `compute_gae_advantage_return()` calls `masked_whiten(advantages, response_mask)` over the full batch.
4. `_update_actor()` passes `ppo_mini_batch_size` to `TrainingWorker.train_mini_batch()`.
5. `TrainingWorker.train_mini_batch()` splits the batch into multiple chunks and calls `train_batch()` once per chunk, but does not re-normalize the advantages for each chunk.

As a result, the full batch has token-weighted advantage mean zero, while each individual optimizer chunk can have a clearly non-zero mean. When the PPO ratio is close to unity, the policy loss of a chunk is approximately:

```text
pg_loss_chunk ≈ -mean(A_chunk)
```

This produces a chunk-level policy-gradient drift term, makes `actor/loss` much larger than expected, and can sharpen the policy too quickly, causing entropy to collapse faster than in trainers where the advantage batch and update batch are aligned.

The current `main` still has this behavior. There is no worker-side per-chunk advantage whitening path in `TrainingWorker.train_mini_batch()`.

### Expected Behavior

For estimators whose original semantics include full-batch advantage whitening, the whitening scope should match the actual optimizer-update scope, or the code should explicitly re-normalize each optimizer chunk before computing its PPO loss.

After the fix, for every optimizer chunk `k`:

- the token-weighted mean of `advantages` over valid response tokens selected by `response_mask` should be approximately zero;
- the token-weighted variance should be approximately unit variance when whitening is enabled;
- the behavior should be equivalent to directly whitening that chunk, even if the full batch was already whitened earlier;
- `returns` should remain unchanged so that critic training still uses the original returns;
- multi-DP-rank runs should use statistics from the global chunk, not independent per-rank statistics.

### Actual Behavior

Only the full advantage batch is whitened. The worker then splits that batch into optimizer chunks without re-normalizing them.

In a controlled synchronous run where the sampled batch was larger than the actor mini-batch, the global `critic/advantages/mean` was close to zero, but individual update chunks had different non-zero advantage means. The resulting `actor/loss` was much larger than in an asynchronous run where the advantage batch and update batch were aligned.

The difference appeared from the earliest update steps while the policies still started from the same checkpoint, so it is consistent with chunk-level advantage bias rather than long-horizon policy drift.

### Reproduction

1. Use the V1 synchronous trainer with GAE and set `actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size` smaller than the sampled batch. Use `loss_agg_mode=token-mean` and disable auxiliary entropy/KL losses.

2. Before each `train_batch()` call in `TrainingWorker.train_mini_batch()`, log the token-weighted advantage mean of the current chunk:

   ```python
   mask = mini_batch_td["response_mask"].bool()
   chunk_adv_mean = mini_batch_td["advantages"][mask].mean().item()
   print("chunk_adv_mean", chunk_adv_mean)
   ```

3. Compare the per-chunk means and the per-chunk `actor/pg_loss` values.

Observed result: the chunk means are not all zero, while their token-weighted combination over the full batch is approximately zero. The per-chunk `pg_loss` follows `-chunk_adv_mean` when the PPO ratio is close to unity.

The same issue can be reproduced with the `colocate_async` trainer when its sampled batch is larger than `ppo_mini_batch_size`. It is not specific to a model architecture, dataset, or FSDP/Megatron backend.

### Root Cause

Relevant code paths in current `main`:

- `verl/trainer/ppo/v1/trainer_base.py`

missions.title: spec(judge,actions): LLM judge step as a non-verdict score (amends §7)
missions.description:
## Overview

Part of #707. The user decided (2026-11-19) that a VD step may call an LLM judge and record its score as a metric that never decides the verdict, so eval tasks can carry rubric scores beside their mechanical criteria in one Duhem report. This changes duhem-spec §7 ("No AI is in the execution loop"), so this spec carries the identity amendment. It must keep the public promise "no LLM in the verdict" mechanically true.

## Design

- A judge step (provisional name `llm/score`) sends a declared rubric plus declared observations (step outputs, files, evidence blobs) to a declared model and records a numeric score, the raw response, the model id and version, and the prompt hash as evidence.
- **Verdict isolation, enforced by `validate` and the runtime, not by convention:** a judge step's outputs can't be referenced from `assertions:`, `if:`, `for_each:` or any `$steps` expression. A judge step contributes no implicit judgment. Its success, failure or timeout never changes the check, criterion, body or effective verdict or the CLI exit code. A failed judge call shows up as a missing score.
- Reports (`--reporter json`, pretty, dashboard) show judge scores in a separate, labelled `scores` block that's never mixed into verdict counts. The Harbor adapter (#707) maps them to `llm_*` reward keys.
- Credentials come from registered secrets and are masked. A run with judge steps needs network access to the model provider. A `--no-judges` flag skips them, so a gate can run without any LLM.
- Pairwise or comparative judging across candidates is out of scope, because a single VD run sees only one candidate.

## Plan

- [ ] Amend duhem-spec §7 and the README wording, with the Alignment rationale below.
- [ ] Add the judge action, the validator isolation rules and the separate `scores` reporting.
- [ ] Add an executable worked example with a stubbed provider in CI, plus a real-provider example run manually.

## Test

- [ ] `validate` rejects every way of referencing a judge output from assertions, `if:`, `for_each:` and expressions.
- [ ] With an identical candidate, verdict and exit code are identical whether the judge returns a high score, a low score, an error or a timeout, or `--no-judges` is set.
- [ ] Reports keep scores out of pass/fail/inconclusive counts; secrets are masked in evidence.

## Schema impact

- **Category:** additive. **Surfaces:** action catalog, evidence, RunSummary (`scores`), validator. **Migration:** none. **CHANGELOG.md entry:** required.

## DX impact

- Action reference/describe, the verification-authoring skill (when a score is acceptable versus a criterion), the worked example, README positioning wording and CHANGELOG.

## Alignment

Amends §7: an LLM may run inside the execution loop, but only as an evidence producer whose output is unreachable by the judge. The verdict stays deterministic over structured assertions, so "no LLM in the verdict" still holds and is enforced by validation. Rationale: eval tasks need subjective quality scores alongside mechanical correctness, and the user chose to keep them in one report. Risk accepted by the user: a score beside a verdict may be read as a grade, so reports must label it as non-verdict. The Duhem PM recommended keeping judges outside Duhem; this spec records the user's contrary decision.

## Notes

User decision source: Duhem PM thread, structured question, 2026-11-19. Related: #707, #582 (deterministic metrics, a different mechanism).

missions.title: Proposal: experimental flag to resend own Notarize/Skip votes to the reward leader
missions.description:
#### Problem A validator loses the vote reward for slot V when the leader of V+8 builds V's reward certificate without that validator's Notarize or Skip vote. Today Agave sends each vote once, as a QUIC datagram, and datagrams are never retransmitted. One lost datagram to one specific peer therefore costs a full slot's reward. On mainnet, validators miss reward slots while their votor connection to the reward leader stays up. Connection loss is not the cause; it is plain datagram loss. Nothing in the protocol recovers it: the vote still counts toward consensus through other peers, but only the V+8 leader's view decides the reward. Firedancer already covers this case: its votor sends a reward vote to the V+8 leader first and retries it until a QUIC ACK covers it, up to 16 sends. On a lossy path, an Agave validator can miss rewards that a Firedancer validator recovers. **Data:** mainnet measurements of missed reward slots per epoch with the flag at 0, 2 and 4, and the matching `votor_reward_resend.*` counters, will follow in a comment. #### Proposed Solution Add an experimental validator flag, `--experimental-reward-vote-copies `, that sends N extra copies (1 to 4) of each of the node's own Notarize and Skip votes to the leader that builds that vote's reward certificate (the leader of `vote_slot + 8`). Copies go by unicast, one every 200 ms after the broadcast: +200, +400, +600 and +800 ms. The flag defaults to 0, so a node without it behaves exactly as today. With the flag on, a reward vote counts whenever any one of its 1 + N sends arrives in time, at a cost of N extra datagrams per vote to one peer. Operators can measure the gain on their own path before anyone proposes a default. The change would land as a stack of three PRs, each reviewable on its own: 1. **Vote-pool invariant test** (`bls-sigverify`): proves that re-sent votes, in any arrival order, are duplicates and never cause a ban. 2. **Unicast send path** (`votor-transport`): send one datagram to one peer over the existing outbound connection, with counters. 3. **Experimental reward-vote resend** (`votor`, `core`, `validator`): the flag, the resend queue with its guards and metrics, and a rate-limit formula that accounts for up to 4 copies (the limit stays 50 pps). ### Background Three parts of current Agave (master `30c1d28642`, 2026-11-19) decide what a resend can do. **When the reward certificate is built.** The leader of V+8 asks its rewards service for V's certificates when it starts producing slot V+8, and the service builds them at once (biased select in `reward_certs_service.rs`). Since #16258 the request is sent before waiting for the parent to replay, in both `produce_first_slot` and `produce_intra_window_slot`. With fast leader handover, the first slot of a window can start on an optimistic parent, before V+8's nominal start. Votes that arrive after the build do not count for V. **Per-peer rate limit.** Each receiver limits every peer to `votor_rate_limit_pps()` = `NEW_PACKETS_PER_SLOT` (6) × 1000 / 200 ms + 20 standstill = **50 pps**, with a 1 s burst bucket (50 tokens). Above that, datagrams are dropped. Only dropped datagrams drain a separate 60 s budget, so a peer is disconnected only when it sends above about twice the rate. **Bans.** The sigverify stage bans a sender only for a conflicting vote (`VotePoolError::Invalid`), a bad signature or a bad certificate. A byte-identical repeat is `VotePoolError::Duplicate` and is dropped before signature verification, counted in `vote_pool_duplicate`. ### Goals and non-goals Goals: - Opt-in only: with the flag at its default of 0, no copy is sent and nothing changes. - With N copies, count a reward vote whenever any one of its 1 + N sends reaches the V+8 leader in time. - Add at most 4 datagrams per vote, sent to one peer only, and stay within that peer's rate limit in the worst case. - Change no wire format, no consensus rule and no receiver behavior; old and new nodes interoperate. - Never send a copy under an identity other than the one that signed the vote. Non-goals: - Recovering from loss bursts of 800 ms or more, or from a dropped connection. The deadline rules out copies late enough to help. - Reliable delivery for Finalize, fallback or genesis votes, or for certificates. They do not decide rewards. - ACK-driven retransmission. It needs per-datagram ACK events that Quinn does not expose (see Alternatives). ### Design overview The broadcast path stays as it is. PR 3 adds a timed queue beside it, PR 2 gives that queue a way to reach one peer over the connection already open, and PR 1 pins down the receiver behavior both rely on. ```mermaid flowchart LR VS["VotingService
